pin_row_note: The ball centre never reaches the pin-base row in a readable frame: at 461 it is level with the pin-deck front (y 1046, pin bases ~1025), at 463 it is ~20 px below the headpin base row (y ~992). From 464 the camera whips and the ball cannot be found (zz_464_467). pin_row_y is the headpin base row at 463.

entry.definition: GUTTER BALL: entry = lateral position in the right gutter beside the pin deck (no pin contact). The pin_hit+1 edge read (464) is unreadable (camera whip) and is missing.

read_notes.pin_ruler_6in_f459: 7 pin columns at x 738..795 (white-profile peaks, checked on z_459_rack8), 9.5 px per 6 in = 1.73 px/board, headpin column 767 = board 20, at the pin-base row 1042; ball is 30 px lower (y 1072) so scale and centre were carried to the ball row by the edge-width ratio 98/83. Physically impossible (13 boards beyond the right edge, the gutter is ~8.5): the rack scale is ~20 % smaller than the edge scale, the same disagreement loop 1 saw.
read_notes.pin_ruler_6in_f461: rack is a blurred bar x 685..755 (7 columns assumed at the ends), ball 21 px below the pin bases; scale carried by edge-width ratio 98.5/84. Weak: the rack extremes are guesses on a motion-blurred frame.

min_board_scope: on-lane points only (f <= 441). The ball is in the right gutter from ~443 (centre crosses the edge at 441); off-lane boards (-2 to -5) move with blur and gutter geometry, not with a hook, so they are excluded from min_board and hooks_back.
method: Every path point was read by eye on gridded crops of the source frame (3x ball crop, 4x edge/gutter zooms, 8x rack zoom) made with cv2 from frames decoded by CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES (checked identical to sequential decode); the left and right lane edges are the wood end at the ball's own row in the same frame, with a Lab b* walker used only to place candidate ticks that were then confirmed or overridden by eye. board = 1 + 38 (x - right_x)/(left_x - right_x) at row y (fields left_x/right_x/board) and again at the contact row y+r (left_x_yr/right_x_yr/board_yr); min_board and hooks_back use the row-y column.
limits: Gutter ball: the ball runs right from board ~12.5 at 418 to the edge at 441 and rides the right gutter to the deck, so the entry board is a gutter position (-2 to -5) and the pin ruler, built for a ball among the pins, does not apply cleanly (one read is physically impossible, one is a guess on blur). From 455 every frame has heavy diagonal motion blur (head turning right), so far-end ball centres are +-4-5 px and edges +-4 px, about +-1.5-2 boards on a 100 px lane; 464+ is unreadable. The right edge beside the ball (436-441) had to be read as a line above and below the ball because the ball covers it. The near-end rows are rolled ~8 deg so a horizontal row is not a perpendicular cut across the lane (sub-board effect). Release 412 confirmed on rel_411_413.jpg (hand over the ball at 411, finger sliver at 412, free at 413).

pin_row.note: Extrapolated, not observed. The ball rolls in the right gutter; at f463 its centre (710, 1012) is still 20 px short of the old base row 992 and ~7 px short of the pin-height base (~1005: pin tops ~965 + 15 in x 2.48 px/in + 3.5 px), moving 10-24 px per frame up the image, so it passes the pin-row depth at f464, where the camera whips and the ball cannot be found (sheet_457_464.jpg, wide_464_500.jpg). Board is the last gutter read (f463); no pin ruler, the ball is outside the pin columns.

contact_note: Gutter ball. The camera whips off the lane from f464 and the deck leaves the view by f472 (wide_464_500.jpg), so no pin motion can be seen; none expected.

exit.deflection: no deck contact: the ball stays in the right gutter to the deck front and is lost in the camera whip
exit.null_reason: never on the pin deck: last seen in the right gutter at the deck front (board -2.69 at f463); from f464 the camera whips away

exit_method: Gutter position read on the camera-followed gridded crops (sheet_457_464.jpg) against the existing path reads; frames after f463 checked on downscaled full frames (wide_464_500.jpg).
exit_limits: Phase-correlation camera shifts after f463 are meaningless (155, -89, 114, 180 px jumps), so no positioned crop exists after f463; frame 464 for the pin-row depth is an extrapolation of the ball's image speed, not an observation.
